<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **36** documentable anchor(s).

**24** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 59d9815a038ed84a8bcdce75df40aeba58ccfaec`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **183** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 59d9815a038ed84a8bcdce75df40aeba58ccfaec` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `445686150360e3e8141f2892d4b6a3335953cd9a` — the merge of head `39a525c236f62c248f1581c8561e1412df05e9e6` into base `59d9815a038ed84a8bcdce75df40aeba58ccfaec`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 445686150360e3e8141f2892d4b6a3335953cd9a && git checkout 445686150360e3e8141f2892d4b6a3335953cd9a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 59d9815a038ed84a8bcdce75df40aeba58ccfaec 39a525c236f62c248f1581c8561e1412df05e9e6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 59d9815a038ed84a8bcdce75df40aeba58ccfaec && git merge --no-ff 39a525c236f62c248f1581c8561e1412df05e9e6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 59d9815a038ed84a8bcdce75df40aeba58ccfaec
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 59d9815a038ed84a8bcdce75df40aeba58ccfaec` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Head-sha: `db650901b620245d2ca5f8dbfb64539af08da3ef`

Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER (Fable, narrowed scope: the ledger hunk + the code implementing the refusal). Verdict: **CHANGES** — 1 must-fix, 2 should-fix, 4 nits. Opus self-review of the rest (CLI `--confirm-upgrade` on `os package install` / `os deploy`, `InstalledManifestEntry` type, changeset, regenerated reference pages): no finding. The `os deploy` pass-through is outside the claim's file surface; the seat accepts it, because ruling (ii) names the CLI flag and the refusal prints `os deploy --confirm-upgrade` as its retry. Size 710 lines, no governed path ⇒ the seat lands it after ACCEPT.

### Findings

**must-fix — the gate admits blind when the installed body is unavailable (P:3779–3786), and the trade-off verdict is: fail-open is not acceptable; fail closed in the narrow, confirmable form below.**
`if (!previousEntry?.manifest) { warn; return {}; }` makes 2c′ the only gate in `handleInstall` that, on an input it cannot read, concludes "no finding" and proceeds. Every sibling refuses or asks again: 2a's datasource-holder check answers 503 because "a check that did not run is never taken for 'no holder'" (P:2554–2566); 2b on a corrupt ledger entry deliberately "ASKS AGAIN rather than skip: the fail-safe direction", with the direction itself pinned (P:2582–2590; `marketplace-install-local-posture-gate.test.ts:237`); 2c answers 503 because "a comparison that did not run is never taken for 'no finding'" (P:3685–3698). Contract (ii) refuses a managed re-install *carrying* a suspected rename or a confirmable type change; with the record unreadable the gate does not know whether it carries one, and the Q3 ruling's own banner at this step is "AN UPGRADE NEVER CHANGES A STORED FIELD SILENTLY" (P:2654–2655) — a `warn` line is the definition of silent for the installer, who gets a 200. The premise "refusing would block the re-install that repairs the record" is only half true and does not cover the whole branch: (a) uninstall, reseed and purge already refuse an unreadable entry 500 with the repair prescription "repair or remove <file>: <cause>" (`unreadableLedgerEntry`, P:6556–6585), so the operator already has a path that is not "re-install blind"; (b) the same branch is also reached on the orphan path — `findConflict` answers `'marketplace'` when `has()` is false but the registry still holds the package (P:4842–4852) — where there is no record at all, and the warn then says "the record of the installed version could not be read", which is false; (c) the warn's prescription "Run the same install with `dryRun: true` to see what the record holds" (P:3783–3784) is wrong: the dry run compares against `undefined` when the entry is unreadable and says so (`installedRecordUnreadable: true`, P:5341–5343, 5357–5362) — it cannot show what the record holds. Concrete fix, no new status and no new code name: pass the ledger lookup (`this.ledger.read(manifestId)`, entry + failure) rather than `.entry` into the gate; when no installed body is available, answer the ordinary `409 SCHEMA_UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` with one finding `{ kind: 'installed_record_unreadable', file, cause, describe }` (orphan path: `kind: 'installed_record_missing'`), its finding-set token digested from that identity, and the same `confirmWith`; the same request with the token installs (the re-install is still the repair), and the ledger entry records `schemaUpgradeConfirmation` — the admission becomes explicit, audited, and one round-trip, exactly 2b's "ask again" direction. An alternative that also satisfies the contract: use the live registry's package body (what `findConflict` step 3 reads) as the installed side, falling to the finding above only when neither exists. Not acceptable: the branch as written, or a 500 à la `unreadableLedgerEntry` (it pushes the operator to delete the file, which lands on the equally blind orphan path). Pin both halves with the existing corrupt-entry fixture (`writeCorruptEntryFor`, `marketplace-install-local-corrupt-ledger.test.ts:147`): the 409 with its finding, and the token install writing the entry. Today the branch has no pin at all.

**should-fix — `destructive` is in the confirmed set (P:538) but no pin exercises it (T:278–286 pins `needs_confirm` only).**
Ablating `'destructive'` from `SCHEMA_UPGRADE_CONFIRMED_CATEGORIES` leaves the suite green, so half of ruling (ii)'s "needs_confirm / destructive" is unpinned. Add one `it`: installed `company: { type: 'text' }` → incoming `company: { type: 'formula' }` (formula is non-stored — T:318 already relies on `score: formula` being non-stored for the `safe` pin), which `typeChangeCategory` classes `destructive` (`package-upgrade-plan.ts:202–207`); assert 409 and `findings[0].category === 'destructive'`.

**should-fix — the "501 even with a token" pin uses a token that cannot match (T:293 `'schema-upgrade:0'`), so the guard it exists for is not exercised.**
The confirmation branch is `declaredRenames.length === 0 && typeof token === 'string' && token === findingSet` (P:3794). For a declared rename with no other finding the real finding set is the digest of `[]`, which a caller can compute; drop the `declaredRenames.length === 0 &&` guard and the test still passes while a real token bypasses C2 and installs over a declared rename. Compute the real token in the test (`'schema-upgrade:' + createHash('sha256').update(JSON.stringify([])).digest('hex').slice(0, 32)`, mirroring P:629–635) and assert 501 with it; the same for the rename+retype case (T:305–312) if you want C2-over-scope-note pinned against a matching token.

**nit — "`true` confirms nothing" is promised in the refusal (P:3853–3855) but not pinned here**, unlike the access gate (`marketplace-install-local-access-upgrade.test.ts:365`). One `it` with `confirmSchemaUpgrade: true` asserting 409 and the stale sentence.

**nit — `logger` is added to `mount`'s return (T:119) and used by no added test.** Either use it (the fail-open branch's warn, if any warn survives finding 1) or drop it.

**nit — C2 says the 501 names 01b (#30885).** The runtime string rightly carries no tracker number (AGENTS.md: refusal prose carries none) and says "once the runtime carries declared renames" (P:3836), but neither the step comment (P:2653–2664) nor the gate's JSDoc (P:3742–3766) cites 01b / #30885, so nothing in the code points a reader at the issue that lifts the 501. Add the citation to the comment, as the file already cites `#30884`.

**nit — the finding-set identity (P:629–633) excludes `manifestId`**, so a token issued for one package's finding set confirms an identical finding set on another package. The access token digests only its summary too (`access-upgrade-report.ts:606–607`), so this is parity, not a defect; folding `manifestId` into the digest is a one-line hardening if wanted.

### Checked and fine

- Spec hunk is exactly one code, `SCHEMA_UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`, under `'@objectstack/cloud-connection'` in sorted position beside the ACCESS sibling (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts:1371–1383`); the mdx gains the one sorted line; `git diff --stat` shows no other `packages/spec` hunk. The ledger comment states its emitter, status, step and CLI reader.
- Token: `schema-upgrade:` + first 32 hex of sha256 (P:531, 634–635), same shape as the access token; digested over identities only (kind/object/field/type/candidates or kind/object/field/from/to/category/renamedFrom), never `describe` or `rows`; identities string-sorted and candidate lists sorted (P:629–633), so order-free and stable across the two bodies; the two refusals and the confirmation all read the same `findingSet`.
- Stale token: an old token against a changed set answers 409 with the fresh set and the stale sentence (P:3853–3855, 3872); pinned T:261–276 including `not.toBe(oldToken)`.
- Safe / removed / seed never refuse: only `suspectedRenames` and `typeChanges` with category in the set become findings (P:600–613); removed fields, removed objects and seeds never enter `findings`; pinned T:314–332 with the plan asserted to contain all three.
- C2 path: a declared rename answers 501 `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` before the token is honoured (P:3794 guard, P:3811–3850), carrying `details.declaredRenames` and the still-owed `findings`; pinned T:288–303 (modulo the should-fix on the token). Both ways forward are named in the 501 (wait for the runtime, or remove `renamedFrom`, rebuild and confirm) and in the 409 (declare `renamedFrom` and rebuild, or confirm with the token) — pinned T:238–239.
- Scope note vs C2 order is coherent: a declared rename that also retypes `needs_confirm` is a `type_change` finding with `renamedFrom` (P:613–627, from `package-upgrade-plan.ts:367–370`), listed in the 501's `details.findings`, and the 501 message says the next refusal will ask for it (P:3841–3843); pinned T:305–312. The 501 is terminal today, so nothing slips.
- No write before the gate: 2b, 2c, 2c′, 2d, 2e, 2e′ are all checks; the first write is step 3's `register` (P:2750), then the ledger (P:2813) and `syncSchemas` (P:2828). Pinned by `register`/`syncSchemas` not called and `ledgerFiles()` unchanged (T:220–244, 288–303).
- Gate runs only for managed re-installs: `conflict === 'marketplace'` (P:2666), after the access gate (P:2647–2651) as C4 requires; a first install is never compared (T:350–355).
- Ledger entry: `schemaUpgradeConfirmation { findingSet, confirmedBy, confirmedAt }` (P:2808; type `local-manifest-source.ts:103`), present in the entry object both ledger writes persist (P:2813, 2866 reuse `entry`); pinned T:246–259; absent when nothing was confirmed (T:331, 341).
- Error shape mirrors `ACCESS_UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` field for field: `success:false`, `error.{code,message,details.{manifestId,findingSet,findings,confirmWith.{body,cli}}}` (P:3861–3886 vs P:3719–3740); the `cli` hint's `--confirm-upgrade` flag exists in the CLI diff.
- C3: `schemaUpgradeVerdict` is pure (no `ctx`, P:592–635) and decides the refusal; environment rows attach only through `readSchemaUpgradeRows` when `manifest.planUpgrade` is a function (P:3901–3903), keyed by the INSTALLED key (`renamedFrom ?? field`, P:3805–3806), matching `package-upgrade-environment.ts:64–65, 186–191`; a failed reading yields `rows: null` and no count sentence (P:3807–3812); without `planUpgrade` the refusal is identical minus `rows` (T:340–345). The confirmation branch returns before any environment read (P:3794 before P:3803).
- Existing dry-run CONTROL re-pointed to a finding-free upgrade (T:166–172) so it still asserts `planUpgrade` not called on the install path — correct, since the gate now reads it on refusals.

## Contract review

Head-sha: `02481a8990`

Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER (Fable delta r2, over the PR's own commits 7d661aa9f5, a274e36e74 and 5c6cd1cfd7; merges of main discounted). Fable verdict **PASS**, with every round-1 item resolved. It raised one new **should-fix**, which the seat adopts as owed before ACCEPT: a declared rename over an unreadable or missing record must keep its 501. The next round is an in-seat delta. Nits are optional.

### Round-1 items

**must-fix — gate admits blind when the installed body is unavailable: RESOLVED (per the seat's ruling, both halves).**
- The fail-open branch and its warn (incl. the false `dryRun: true` prescription) are gone: `grep` for the old sentences finds nothing in P. The no-body case now goes through `installedRecordUnavailableVerdict` (P:685–705) and the ordinary 409 (P:3933–3966).
- Unreadable ledger entry: `handleInstall` passes the whole lookup (`previousLookup`, P:2669–2670) into the gate (P:2739); `previous.failure` set ⇒ `installedBody` undefined (P:3864–3866) ⇒ one finding `{ kind: 'installed_record_unreadable', file, cause, describe }` (P:690–697; type P:576–584), token digested from `[manifestId, [['installed_record_unreadable', file]]]` (P:659–676), same `confirmWith` (P:3959–3962), same confirmation branch (P:3872–3880) ⇒ the token installs and the ledger entry records `schemaUpgradeConfirmation` (P:2882). Pinned C:354–387 with the existing `writeCorruptEntryFor` fixture: 409, finding kind/file/cause, token shape, `register` not called, the file still unreadable after the refusal, then the token ⇒ 200, `entry.version === '1.0.1'`, `schemaUpgradeConfirmation.findingSet` equal to the issued token. Reachability checked: `findConflict` step 1 answers `'marketplace'` on `has()` (the corrupt file exists, P:4919), 2b passes (GOOD_MANIFEST declares no unique), 2c passes (no access-check service in that fixture ⇒ warn + `{}`, P:3729–3736), so 2c′ is the first refusal.
- Orphan path (ledger `{ entry: null }`, registry still serves the package): the installed side is `registeredPackageBody` (P:3864–3865, P:4949–4957), i.e. the row `findConflict` step 3 matches (`manifestIdOf(p) === manifestId`, P:4937–4940 vs P:4952), converted forward like a ledger body (P:3866). Comparison side is right: the registry's `package` row stores `toRecordManifest(converted body)` (objectql `installPackage`, registry.ts ≈2474 — a JSON projection that keeps `objects`, `fields[].type`, `data`; drops only functions/exotics), so `packageUpgradeSideOf` (P:708–710) folds the same `objects`/`data` as it folds for a ledger body, and `comparePackageVersions` sees the same field types — no false `type_change`/`suspected_rename` from the body's provenance, and a field without `type` on either side yields no type change (plan `typeOf`), never a finding. The second `convertPackageBodyForward` over an already-converted body is a no-op replay (forward conversions rewrite retired shapes only). Pinned T:311–329: a retype against the registry's body is 409 `needs_confirm` with no write; CONTROL: the same orphan with an added field only ⇒ 200 and no `schemaUpgradeConfirmation`.
- Only when neither yields a body: `installed_record_missing` (P:698–702; type P:585–589), token from `[manifestId, [['installed_record_missing']]]`; pinned T:331–349 (409, kind, token equals the restated digest, `register`/`planUpgrade` not called, ledger empty, then token ⇒ 200 with `confirmedBy: INSTALLER`).
- The existing orphan test still passes by reading: `marketplace-install-local-conflict.test.ts:93–112` registers `{ manifest: MANIFEST(id,'1.0.0') }` with `objects: []` and upgrades to the same empty `objects` ⇒ plan empty ⇒ `{}` ⇒ 200.

**should-fix — `destructive` unpinned: RESOLVED.** T:301–309 installs `company: text → formula`, asserts 409 and `category: 'destructive'`; ablating `'destructive'` from the confirmed set now fails a pin.

**should-fix — the "501 even with a token" pins used a token that cannot match: RESOLVED.** T:283–285 restates the digest (`[VENDOR, identities.map(JSON.stringify).sort()]`, matching P:659–676 exactly), T:287–291 proves the helper equals the door's token on a real finding set, T:360–378 sends `tokenFor([])` — the real token of the empty set — and still asserts 501 (dropping the `declaredRenames.length === 0` guard at P:3873 would now install and fail the pin), T:380–388 sends the real `type_change` token on the rename+retype case and asserts 501 with the finding listed.

**nit — `true` confirms nothing unpinned: RESOLVED** (T:293–299, asserts 409, the sentence, no `register`).
**nit — unused `logger` in `mount`'s return: RESOLVED** (T:123 no longer returns it).
**nit — cite 01b/#30885: RESOLVED** (step comment P:2731, JSDoc P:3835–3836).
**nit — `manifestId` in the digest: RESOLVED** (P:659–676, documented at P:608–611 and P:662–663; pinned implicitly by T:287–291 since `tokenFor` folds `VENDOR`).

### New findings (delta)

**should-fix — on the unreadable/missing path a declared rename loses its 501 (P:704, `declaredRenames: []`).** `installedRecordUnavailableVerdict` always answers an empty rename list, so an incoming body that carries `renamedFrom` over an unreadable record is refused 409 `installed_record_unreadable`, and its token installs it — a new field that starts empty while the values stay in the old column, which is the install C2 says "no token answers". The comparison cannot prove the rename applies (it needs the installed key), but a `renamedFrom` declaration with an unknown installed side is exactly a rename this runtime *may* be unable to carry, and the fail-closed direction the rest of this PR adopts says: refuse it as a declared rename. Fix: in `installedRecordUnavailableVerdict` (or just before it in the gate), scan `packageUpgradeSideOf(converted).objects` for fields with a non-empty `renamedFrom` array and return them as `declaredRenames` (`{ object, from: renamedFrom[0], to: key, toType }`, `fromType` omitted), so the existing 501 branch (P:3897–3931) fires with the finding listed beside it; the 409 keeps its one finding when no rename is declared. Pin in C beside C:360: the corrupt fixture + `fields: { name2: { type: 'text', renamedFrom: ['name'] } }` ⇒ 501 `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, token or not. The seat may rate this must-fix; I rate it should-fix because the admission is explicit and the 409 sentence does say "cannot be checked for fields it renames".

**nit — `installed_record_missing` is also answered when the ledger entry parses but carries no `manifest` (P:3864–3868).** `previous.entry?.manifest ?? (...)` falls to `installedRecordUnavailableVerdict(manifestId, undefined)` there, whose describe says the runtime "holds no record of the installed version's package body" — true enough, but the kind's own doc (P:586) and the gate JSDoc (P:3827–3832) describe `missing` as the orphan case only. Either widen the two comments ("…or a record carrying no body") or name the file: pass `previous.entry ? { file: safeFilename(manifestId), cause: 'the entry carries no manifest' } : previous.failure`.

**nit — the cause string is derived by hand twice (P:692, 694) while `describeLedgerCause` (P:1169–1171) exists for exactly this**, and the hand version turns an `Error` with an empty `message` into `""` where the helper falls back to `name`. Use the helper once into a local.

**nit — multi-package orphan folds a partial installed side.** The `manifest` service registers one registry row per `packages[]` entry (objectql `plugin.ts:854+`), so for a `packages[]` artifact the row `registeredPackageBody` finds under the artifact's `manifest.id` — when one exists at all — holds one package's body, while `converted` folds every package's objects; sibling packages then read as "added objects" and a retype inside them is a false negative on the orphan path only (the ledger path folds the whole artifact). Not a regression (db650901 was fully blind here) and beyond the ruling's wording, so a nit: fold the rows of every id in `resolveArtifactPackageEntries(converted)` that the registry holds, or state the limitation in the JSDoc at P:4943–4948.

### Checked and fine

- No write precedes the gate: 2c′ (P:2737–2742) still runs before step 3's `register` (P:2822), the ledger write (P:2882) and `syncSchemas`; `registeredPackageBody` and `readSchemaUpgradeRows` only read; pinned by `register` not called and `ledgerFiles()` unchanged in every new refusal pin (T:318–319, T:339–341, C:375).
- The unreadable path cannot be bypassed: `installedBody` is undefined whenever `previous.failure` is set (the `??` right operand requires `failure === undefined`, P:3865), the verdict then always has one finding, and the only admit is `token === findingSet` (P:3873). Its token cannot confirm another situation: identities `['installed_record_unreadable', file]` / `['installed_record_missing']` share no digest with any comparison set or with each other, and `manifestId` is folded in; `cause` is deliberately outside the identity so a differently-worded parse error yields the same token for the same file.
- `rows` are never read without an installed body (P:3883), and the row-count decoration skips the two new kinds (P:3885); the 501 branch, the stale sentence and the 409 shape are unchanged for comparison findings; the no-body 409 message drops the `renamedFrom` advice, rightly (P:3937–3940).
- `registeredPackageBody` typing (5c6cd1cfd7): `OverrideGateEngine.registry.getAllPackages?(): unknown` (P:834–839) narrowed by `Array.isArray`; `manifestIdOf(p: any)` accepts the `unknown` element; `ctx.getService<T>` is the generic already used at P:1489, 1987, 2345.
